liam_z: FYI seeing a reg on nightly after the kernel-selector tweak — ~+30% p50 token latency on the synthetic long-seq job. attaching traces (nsys + perfetto) and a short nvprof snippet. :eyes:

liam_z: nsys: s3://redwood-perf/3925001234/nightly-before-after.nsys
perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/3925001234
quick nvprof excerpt:
```
GPU time: kernel_A 0.9ms (baseline) -> kernel_B 1.7ms (nightly)
CUDA memcpy HtoD spikes at 2.1ms, appears aligned with KV refill windows
```

nisha_k: which workload + seq len? is this the 512-token chat-runner or longcontext bench? also please re-run with NVTX markers around kv read/write so we can see boundaries. :thinking:

liam_z: repro is longcontext-512 (batch=1, temp=0.0). I already grabbed traces with nvtx markers enabled (runner has them). the timeline shows a scheduler/kernel switch right before big memcpy islands at ~step 4-5. impression: selector picks fallback kernel_B for some batches causing extra memcopies.

sarah_h: can you paste the command you used to collect nsys? also add --sample=none to get full timeline if you didn't. if we can reproduce quickly we should git-bisect the selector change. suggestion: keep a minimized runner (no logging) and capture two traces (force kernel A vs default) to validate causality.

liam_z: cmd I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn --output out.nsys ./tools/runner --model longcontext --seq 512 --batch 1 --warmup 20 --steps 50
```

daniel_r: quick look at the flame: GPU occupancy drops ~18% on nightly, SM stalls up, and memcpy HtoD takes ~14% of wall time where before it was ~2-3%. That smells like additional KV refills or a host-side staging path triggered by kernel change. check prefetch_window and kv-eviction logs. Also look at kernel grid/block for kernel_B — it has more small launches which hurts occupancy.

liam_z: paste from nsys timeline (condensed):
```
[0.0s] kernel_A (selected) -> steady
[0.9s] KV read (device) -> cache hit
[nightly] selector heur -> kernel_B
[1.7s] kernel_B -> issues
[1.72s] cudaMemcpy HtoD (large) repeated x3
```

perf-bot: Job 4837 finished: artifacts uploaded s3://redwood-perf/3925001234/out.nsys :white_check_mark:

nisha_k: quick mitigation: force kernel A via env flag and run a quick comparison. if p50 drops back we can be confident selector change is root cause. env: export RW_KERNEL_SELECTOR_OVERRIDES=kernel_A. also add RW_PREFETCH_WINDOW=3 to test kv-prefetching impact.

liam_z: forced run done — p50 back to baseline, memcpy islands disappear in perfetto. occupancy restored. so selector decision is likely flipping when sequence segmentation boundary occurs. I'll bisect the kernel-selector changes between commit ab12f3c..cf34e91 (those include the scoring refactor + a tiny prefetch tweak). planning: git bisect with a small reproducer and capture nsys per step. anyone want to pair on the bisect script?

sarah_h: please add the branch and a short summary to the eng-runtime backlog (put the traces + forced-run artifacts). tag sel-heuristics owners (cc @nisha_k) and mark a hotfix if bisect finds a clear regression. also add the perf numbers to the incident doc.

daniel_r: if bisect points to scoring refactor we should also run microbench for kernel scoring costs — maybe the new cost model biases toward lower-occupancy kernel_B for edge cases. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

liam_z: will start bisect tonight and drop interim traces to s3; ping me if you want to watch. thanks all. :thumbsup:
